contexts: unit guideline and teaching day, spring 2027
reading: Family diaries sit between the intensive care stay and the follow-up clinic: relatives write during the stay, and the diary is meant to help the patient rebuild a coherent account of what happened when it is read later. The retrieved evidence links diaries to fewer patients with high post-traumatic stress symptoms in one trial, but the pooled effect is fragile and almost no study isolates family-written entries. Reading is itself an exposure with a short-lived distress cost and a risk for patients who already have high symptoms. Who is offered a diary depends on language and on family presence, and programmes depend on a lead nurse.
